Subject: CedarWorks SSO/SCIM/IP gating — handoff & execution checkpoints

Hi Alice / CedarWorks infra team,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Looping in Monica (CS lead) and Ben (implementation eng) to transition to execution. We want to lock the minimal gating sequence so we can book the go-live window next week. High-level asks:

- SSO: please confirm identity provider (Okta/AzureAD/GSuite) and share SAML metadata or an IdP metadata URL.
- SCIM: are you planning group sync or user-only? If groups, please share a sample group attribute mapping.
- IP allowlist: we need your NAT egress ranges for the cutover and a tentative firewall window (start/end).
- Service accounts: confirm which downstream systems need dedicated service accounts and any naming conventions.

I attached an editable mutual action plan that breaks these out into owner/date. If you can reply with the SAML metadata and a primary infra contact for firewall changes, Ben will draft the SCIM mapping and test plan.

Attachments: [mutual_action_plan_CedarWorks.xlsx]

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30 min sync once we have the metadata.

— Priyom

Subject: Re: CedarWorks SSO/SCIM/IP gating — handoff & execution checkpoints

Priyom / team — thanks, happy to move forward. Quick answers:

- IdP: Okta (org: cedarworks.okta.com). Attached is our SAML metadata XML and the assertion consumer URL we use.
- SCIM: we want groups + users. Primary source is our HRIS -> Okta; we'll want group membership for role-based access in the Redwood Console. See a short sample CSV attached for attributes we typically sync.
- IP allowlist: we can carve an outbound maintenance window. Our network team needs the Redwood egress ranges and ideally 24–48h lead time for firewall change.
- Service accounts: we need a single service account for provisioning and a separate read-only account for observability. Naming convention: cedarw-redwood-<env>-svc.

Attached: [cedarworks_saml_metadata.xml], [scim_sample_groups.csv]

Procurement note: Procurement expects the IP change window to be scheduled two weeks out — is there any flexibility on your side?

Alice Tan
Director, Infrastructure | CedarWorks
alice.tan@cedarworks.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Alice Tan <alice.tan@cedarworks.com>, Infra Team <infra@cedarworks.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CedarWorks SSO/SCIM/IP gating — handoff & execution checkpoints

Thanks Alice — that is helpful. Quick implementation plan / checklist from infra side:

1) SAML setup (Day 0–1)
   - I will upload the IdP metadata to the Redwood Console and configure the ACS and EntityID per your file.
   - Confirm NameID format (email vs persistent); prefer email.

2) SCIM mapping & staging (Day 1–3)
   - I’ll create a staging tenant and run a dry-run sync with your sample groups.
   - Need confirmation of the SCIM base URL and an SCIM admin token. We will provide a short curl test we ask you to run from your network to validate reachability.

3) IP allowlist & cutover (Day 4)
   - Please allowlist these Redwood egress CIDRs: 34.120.16.0/20, 44.56.128.0/20 (these are our staging ranges).
   - For production cutover we’ll provide final egress and a 4-hour maintenance window. Ben will coordinate exact times with your infra lead.

4) Service accounts & perms (parallel)
   - Provision two service accounts as Alice outlined. We will require their public key or client id depending on auth mode.

5) Smoke tests & rollback plan (Day 5)
   - Verify sign-in, group-based entitlements, API provisioning flows. Rollback: revert allowlist change and switch to local fallback auth for up to 1 hour.

I’ll prepare a short runbook and drop it in the Drive link Priyom shared once Alice confirms the SCIM admin token approach.

— Ben
Ben Carter | Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment referenced: scim_mapping_v1.csv]
